ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is the best answer to 'When does the match begin?' (1 mark)
   A. At ten o'clock.
   B. On the field.
   C. It is mine.
   D. The referee.

2. What does 'scanning' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Drawing a picture
   B. Copying the text
   C. Looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number
   D. Reading every word slowly

3. How long should you rub your hands when washing them, according to the text? (1 mark)
   A. There is no time needed
   B. About twenty seconds
   C. About ten minutes
   D. About two seconds

4. When do we say 'I beg your pardon'? (1 mark)
   A. When we are hungry
   B. When we did not hear or we need to say sorry
   C. When we win
   D. When we say goodbye

5. Which describes the letter b? (1 mark)
   A. A stick that goes below the line
   B. A round part with the stick on its right
   C. A dot only
   D. A stick with the round part on its right

6. Which is a good rule for writing an SMS? (1 mark)
   A. Send it to strangers
   B. Leave out your name
   C. Be polite, short and clear
   D. Use secret code

7. When reading silently, you should (1 mark)
   A. sing
   B. shout
   C. read quietly in your head
   D. read backwards

8. A dialogue is (1 mark)
   A. a list of nouns
   B. a picture only
   C. a poem with no words
   D. a conversation between two or more people

9. Which sentence is joined correctly? (1 mark)
   A. We swept the floor, for we wiped the desks.
   B. We swept the floor, nor we wiped the desks.
   C. We swept the floor, and we wiped the desks.
   D. We swept the floor, yet we wiped the desks.

10. Which words link one picture to the next? (1 mark)
   A. mango, rice, milk
   B. red, blue, green
   C. first, then, at last
   D. big, small, tall

11. What is a signature? (1 mark)
   A. Your date of birth
   B. Your grade
   C. Your name written in your own handwriting
   D. Your telephone number

12. An underpass is (1 mark)
   A. a bicycle
   B. a bridge over a river
   C. a kind of train
   D. a path or road that goes under a busy road

13. What must a diary entry begin with? (1 mark)
   A. A question
   B. A title in capitals
   C. A friend's name
   D. The day and date

14. Which are pests? (1 mark)
   A. Sacks for storing maize
   B. Tools for digging
   C. Small animals or insects that damage crops
   D. Tall trees

15. Target sounds: Which word has the sound /aɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. invite
   B. farm
   C. turn
   D. noise

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Give two reasons why we should read widely. (2 marks)

17. Name the three groups of food on a healthy plate and give one example of each. (3 marks)

18. When is it right to interrupt a speaker, and how should you do it? (3 marks)

19. Explain what Baraka learnt from his grandmother. (4 marks)

20. What is a nonverbal cue? Give two examples. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — At ten o'clock.
   'When' asks for a time.

2. C — Looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number
   Scanning searches for specific information.

3. B — About twenty seconds
   Rub for about twenty seconds, then rinse.

4. B — When we did not hear or we need to say sorry
   It asks a person to repeat or says sorry.

5. D — A stick with the round part on its right
   For b the stick is on the left and the round part on the right.

6. C — Be polite, short and clear
   A good SMS is clear and polite.

7. C — read quietly in your head
   Silent reading helps you focus.

8. D — a conversation between two or more people
   It shows what people say to each other.

9. C — We swept the floor, and we wiped the desks.
   'And' adds an idea.

10. C — first, then, at last
   They are linking words for order.

11. C — Your name written in your own handwriting
   A signature shows that you agree with what is written.

12. D — a path or road that goes under a busy road
   Pedestrians can walk through it without meeting cars.

13. D — The day and date
   Every entry is dated.

14. C — Small animals or insects that damage crops
   Pests eat or damage crops.

15. A — invite
   Invite has /aɪ/ in its second syllable.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary and improves reading speed and understanding. It gives knowledge and enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy foods such as ugali; body-building foods such as beans; protective foods such as spinach.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with an example.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: When you did not hear or understand, or someone needs urgent help. Say politely: 'Excuse me, may I say something?'
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the reasons and 1 for a polite phrase.

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: He learnt that ugali and tea are not enough. A balanced diet with energy foods, body-building foods, fruit and vegetables and clean water keeps a person strong and healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct points.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: A nonverbal cue is a message sent without words. Examples: a smile shows happiness; a thumbs-up shows approval.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 for each example.
